question: True or false: people grateful to someone who had just helped them were also readier to help a total stranger?
answer: True. Bartlett and DeSteno staged a computer crash that a helpful stranger fixed. Grateful participants later spent more time on a tedious favour, even when the person asking was someone new rather than their helper. Gratitude did not just repay a debt; it spread to a newcomer.
move: Kindness received tends to be passed on, not just paid back.
ask: Who helped me recently, and whom could I pass that help on to this week?
trap: Assuming gratitude is repaid only to the person who helped.
reference: Bartlett & DeSteno, Gratitude and prosocial behavior: helping when it costs you, Psychological Science, 2006
